relation: Q(t)=b+mt; dQ/dt=m; V(t)−V(0)=bt+mt²/2. Use the signed difference of the antiderivative at the two cursors. Initial inventory zero for the default example.
method: Closed-form evaluation plus exact primitive; for secant width h>0 clip endpoints to domain. Sample 101 x coordinates only for rendering.
limits: Linear ramp, continuous commanded flow; reject a>t. Negative Q is an outward flow, suppress a physical fill animation if the integral demands negative inventory. Compare sampled trapezoids and noisy forward differences.

relation: A=πD²/4; v=Q/A; ṁ=ρQ. Two stations share Q by steady incompressible continuity. Positive axial direction downstream. Density fixed at 1000 kg/m³.
method: Compute both areas before velocities. Draw arrow lengths proportional to v on one legend and use a labelled scale change when space runs out.
limits: One-dimensional steady single-phase flow in an impermeable branch-free pipe; acceleration profile and required pressure unknown. For compressible flow use constant ṁ and solve densities from a thermodynamic model.

relation: dp/dz=−ρg with z upward; p_abs=p_surface+ρgh for depth h down from the free surface. g=9.80665 m/s²; local atmosphere for gauge display fixed at 101325 Pa.
method: Compute p_abs first and subtract atmosphere once. Convert Pa to kPa for display. Width toggle doubles width with no recalculation of pressure.
limits: Static, uniform-density liquid, uniform gravity, negligible capillarity. Layered fluids require piecewise integration; gas columns require a density model. Pressure is scalar; arrows on walls indicate normal traction only.

relation: p₂=p₁+ρg[z₁−z₂+hₚ−hL]+ρ(v₁²−v₂²)/2; vᵢ=4Q/(πDᵢ²); hL=K v₂²/(2g). z₁=0; ρ=1000 kg/m³; g=9.80665 m/s². K referenced to station 2; kinetic energy factors both one.
method: Calculate continuity → kinetic heads → losses → absolute outlet pressure. Optional teaching-water vapour-pressure input from a named property record; default unspecified. Unknown margin is distinct from energy-balance failure.
limits: Steady incompressible single-phase flow, common streamline or section-average with declared factors; K is lumped. Ideal mode locks hp and K at zero. If calculated absolute pressure reaches vapour pressure suppress liquid prediction; absent temperature/vapour data flag unknown cavitation margin.

relation: u(r)=2v̄[1−(r/R)²]; v̄=Q/(πR²); Δp/L=8μv̄/R²; τrz=μ du/dr=−4μv̄r/R²; Re=2ρRv̄/μ. ρ=1000 kg/m³.
method: Evaluate the analytic solution on a symmetric radius grid including 0 and wall. Cross-check 2π∫u r dr=Q using numerical quadrature; stationary state returns zero gradients.
limits: Newtonian, no slip, circular, fully developed and laminar. Accept fully developed geometry as an explicit scenario premise; transitional Re suppresses prediction unless labelled ideal mathematical comparison. Entrance flow needs developing-profile data.

relation: η=y√(U/(νx)); f‴+½ f f″=0, f(0)=f′(0)=0, f′(∞)=1; u/U=f′; Reₓ=Ux/ν; δ₉₉≈4.91√(νx/U); τw=.33206ρU²/√Reₓ; Cf,x=.6641/√Reₓ, mean Cf=1.3282/√ReL. ReL=UL/ν uses plate length, not an average Reynolds number.
method: Cache dimensionless similarity table. Shoot hydrodynamic wall slope or use a reviewed table, integrate thermal BVP with same f for each Pr. Find first .99 crossing by interpolation. Quadruple x within the laminar domain for scaling test.
limits: Steady smooth isothermal flat plate, attached laminar incompressible zero-pressure-gradient flow, uniform upstream velocity, constant properties. x≤L; x=0 singular. Reₓ near 5×10⁵ is a teaching screen, transition depends on surface and disturbance. Do not extrapolate Blasius to separation or use turbulent profiles near the wall as shear estimates.

relation: Re=ρvD/μ=vD/ν; constant-Q mode derives v=4Q/(πD²). Default prescribed-speed mode. For external flow replace D with distance from the leading edge and use free-stream U.
method: Lock one of speed and flow for each mode. Carry SI pair at mode change to avoid jumping operating point. Evaluate geometry-specific labels after calculation.
limits: Pipe screen Re<2300, 2300–4000 transitional, >4000 commonly turbulent for developed Newtonian flow; disturbance can alter onset. Thresholds belong to geometry, never reuse pipe labels for plates, impellers or beds.

relation: v=4Q/(πD²); Δp=fD (L/D)ρv²/2 where fD is the Darcy factor; laminar fD=64/Re; turbulent 1/√fD=−2log₁₀[ε/(3.7D)+2.51/(Re√fD)]. ρ=1000 kg/m³, μ=.001 Pa·s.
method: Analytical laminar branch or bracketed scalar turbulent implicit residual. Test exact endpoints around 2300/4000. For Q=0 skip log/reciprocal. Display a gap and reason for each unmodelled condition.
limits: Full, straight, developed Newtonian liquid, constant bore. Laminar <2300; transition 2300–4000 suppress point estimate; turbulent ≥4000 within curated envelope Re≤10⁷ and ε/D≤.05. These upper limits are product guards, not a measured accuracy envelope. At Q=0 output Δp=0 and f undefined.

relation: Hₚ=s²H₀−aQ²; Hs=Hz+bQ²; Q*=√[(s²H₀−Hz)/(a+b)] when numerator positive. Shaft power=ρgQH/η only with specified efficiency. Synthetic centrifugal curve; Q in m³/s. g=9.80665, ρ=1000.
method: Evaluate physical numerator before sqrt. Draw curves only within declared domains. For optional measured points use monotone segmented interpolation within data hull and identify each genuine crossing independently.
limits: Illustrative quadratic curves, similar hydraulic operation. Limit to forward flow and Hₚ≥0; no positive duty if shutoff ≤ lift. Real power/efficiency, allowable flow, motor limits and NPSH need independent vendor curves. Same-speed measured data do not validate affinity extrapolation.

relation: A=πD²/4; v=Q/A; Hreq=Δz+(fL/D+ΣK)v²/(2g); Pshaft=ρgQHreq/η. Use prescribed Darcy f for first release; advanced mode delegates to the friction block. ρ=1000, g=9.80665.
method: Enumerate bores; compute each loss term. With S09 default H₀=10,a=10⁶ solve s=√[(Hreq+aQ²)/H₀]. Screen .4≤s≤1.2. Optional annual kWh=Pshaft hours/(1000ηmotor).
limits: Steady incompressible water; provided f is a scenario assumption. Bore is actual internal diameter. Vendor efficiency, NPSHR, allowable operation, material compatibility, pipe rating and site elevations required before selection.

relation: R″=L₁/k₁+Rc″+L₂/k₂; q″=(Th−Tc)/R″; Q̇=Aq″; interface faces Th−q″L₁/k₁ and Tc+q″L₂/k₂. Positive heat flux left to right; isothermal external faces; A=1 m².
method: Accumulate temperature drops in the signed heat direction; derive left and right contact temperatures separately. Each layer is a piecewise linear segment, with two coordinates at a contact jump.
limits: 1-D steady conduction with no generation, uniform A, piecewise constant k, negligible edge losses. Single-layer preset removes second layer and its contact. Alternative k(T) requires ∫k(T)dT and matched interface flux; transient case needs ρcp and IC.

relation: Rcond=ln(ro/ri)/(2πkL); Rconv=1/(2πrohL); Q̇=(Ti−T∞)/(Rcond+Rconv); rc=k/h; T(r)=Ti−Q̇ ln(r/ri)/(2πkL). L=1 m. Fixed inner surface temperature.
method: Use log1p(d/ri), include d=0. In inverse mode bracket [ri,rc] and [max(ri,rc),ri+dmax] only when each interval exists. Deduplicate tangent solution.
limits: Long cylinder, constant k and h, no ends/radiation/contact. For ri≥rc heat loss decreases monotonically for Ti>T∞. Real h may change with diameter; critical radius is a maximum of heat loss magnitude for fixed driving temperature.

relation: Infinite slab of half-thickness L, two identical convecting faces, Lc=V/As=L. Bi=hL/k, α=k/(ρcp), Fo=αt/L²; lumped T=T∞+(Ti−T∞)exp[−h t/(ρcp L)]. For distributed comparator solve ∂T/∂t=αTxx; Tx(0)=0, −kTx(L)=h(Ts−T∞), initial T=Ti. ρcp=2.0×10⁶ J/(m³ K).
method: Exact lumped branch. Spatial comparator: N=40 equal cells across half slab, backward Euler tridiagonal system; compare N=80 and half Δt. Initialise all cells at Ti; compute surface temperature from face resistance, not last cell centre.
limits: Constant properties, convection on both faces, symmetric uniform initial condition, fluid at fixed temperature. Bi<.1 customary lumped screen; approaching/exceeding requires spatial comparison. Finite-volume implicit balance with actual face convection and half-cell conduction in series; refine grid/time.

relation: Uniform wall T, laminar plate: Reₓ=Ux/ν; Nuₓ=.332 Reₓ^½ Pr^⅓; NūL=.664 ReL^½ Pr^⅓; hx=Nuₓ kf/x; h̄=NūL kf/L; Q̇=h̄WL(Tw−T∞). W=1 m, x=L for default local result, ν=1.5×10⁻⁵ m²/s, kf=.026 W/(m K). Coefficients approximate similarity solution.
method: Use average formula for total duty, local at x=L for trailing edge. If Pr or property provenance unknown display conditional result only; disable extrapolated duty in design.
limits: External smooth isothermal flat plate, attached, low-speed, negligible natural convection, axial conduction and viscous dissipation; constant properties at a film state. Conservatively restrict Pr .6–10 and ReL<5×10⁵ with known laminar premise; unknown disturbance/transition remains explicit. Mixed convection requires buoyancy information.

relation: Ch=ṁh cp,h; Cc=ṁc cp,c; Cr=Cmin/Cmax; N=UA/Cmin; εparallel=[1−exp(−N(1+Cr))]/(1+Cr); εcounter=[1−exp(−N(1−Cr))]/[1−Cr exp(−N(1−Cr))]. At Cr=1 counter ε=N/(1+N). Q̇=εCmin(Thi−Tci); Tho=Thi−Q̇/Ch, Tco=Tci+Q̇/Cc.
method: Use stable expm1 expressions, branch at Cr=1. For profiles integrate dTh/dA=−U(Th−Tc)/Ch and dTc/dA=±U(Th−Tc)/Cc with coflow +, counterflow − in hot-flow coordinate; impose proper inlet boundary for each.
limits: Steady adiabatic exchanger, constant U and capacity rates, single phase, no axial mixing. Require Thi>Tci in heating exercise. Handle nearly equal capacity rates with expm1 and analytic limit. Fouling uses 1/Udirty=1/Uclean+Rf″ on a common area basis.

relation: From target Q̇ calculate terminal temperatures using Ch,Cc. For counterflow ΔT₁=Thi−Tco, ΔT₂=Tho−Tci; for parallel use inlet and outlet differences. ΔTlm=(ΔT₁−ΔT₂)/ln(ΔT₁/ΔT₂), limit ΔT₁=ΔT₂. A=Q̇/(Udirty ΔTlm); 1/Udirty=1/Uclean+Rf″.
method: Screen εmax using layout before log. Near equal differences use log1p or exact limit; check result by forward NTU calculation. No finite result at pinch.
limits: Ideal two-stream single-phase exchanger only. Positive approaches required; 0 duty → 0 area, limiting duty requires infinite area. Shell-and-tube correction factors require a separately specified geometry; Δp, vibration, allowable pressure and fouling service need vendor work.

relation: Steady J=−D(C₂−C₁)/L. Semi-infinite transient C(x,t)=Ci+(Cs−Ci)erfc[x/(2√(Dt))], C(0,t)=Cs, C(∞,t)=Ci. In transient mode C₁=Cs and C₂=Ci; at t=0 handle surface jump separately.
method: Use vetted erfc routine or approximation with max absolute error 10⁻⁶ on [0,6], tending to zero thereafter. At t=0 branch interior and imposed surface value explicitly.
limits: One-dimensional constant diffusivity, dilute stationary medium, no reaction/advection. Membrane partition coefficients unity for this exercise. A semi-infinite front is inapplicable once far boundary matters; compare finite-domain solver at long times.

relation: d(Ah)/dt=Qin−Qout. Default pumped outlet at fixed Qout; h=h₀+(Qin−Qout)t/A. Alternative gravity Qout=Cd Ao√(2gh), g=9.80665 m/s², Cd=.62, Ao=.0002 m². Empty/full events at h=0,H=2 m. Stop at first boundary and report remaining requested duration.
method: Analytic pumped outlet, event time from linear root. Gravity mode use RK4 with event interpolation or bracketed integration, stop at boundary; integrate actual cumulative inflow and outflow for conservation.
limits: Perfectly incompressible liquid, constant cross section, gravity or commanded discharge, vented headspace; gravity requires free discharge at datum. Adaptive time integration with event location for gravity mode; do not clip and discard volume.

relation: V dC/dt=Q(Cin−C)−kVC; D=Q/V; C∞=D Cin/(D+k); C(t)=C∞+(C₀−C∞)exp[−(D+k)t]. Fixed volume, equal inlet/outlet. Conservative tracer k=0.
method: Piecewise-constant input segments propagate exact exponential from last state. Editing initial conditions resets run, changing feed while running starts a new segment and preserves state.
limits: Isothermal irreversible first order, ideally mixed, fixed V and Q, density constant. For changing flow/temperature integrate balances; transport lag and dead volume require independent tracer/sensor tests.

relation: For −rA=kCA, constant density: XC=kτ/(1+kτ); XP=1−exp(−kτ); VC=(Q/k)X/(1−X); VP=−(Q/k)ln(1−X). Plot FA0/(−rA)=Q/[k(1−X)] against conversion. τ=V/Q.
method: Performance takes V and computes both X values; design takes X and computes both V values. Use log1p(−X) and expm1. Exclude X=1 from finite sizing.
limits: First-order irreversible isothermal reaction, ideal mixing or ideal plug flow. Conversion ranking conditional on rate law; evaluate full integral for inhibition, reversible and variable-density cases. X is calculated in performance mode, V calculated in design.

relation: k(T)=kref exp[−Ea/R(1/T−1/Tref)]; slope of ln(k/kref) vs 1/T=−Ea/R. R=8.314462618 J/(mol K). Reference parameterisation reduces arbitrary prefactor scales.
method: Evaluate log ratio first and exponentiate only within finite numeric domain. Derivatives optional: dlnk/dT=Ea/(RT²). Display activation energy in kJ/mol, convert explicitly.
limits: Fixed mechanism and activation energy in declared interval. Default synthetic teaching constants; physical range unknown for an unspecified reaction. Do not infer an industrial reaction rate from them.

relation: Ideal binary at one fixed illustrative temperature, PsatA=2×10⁵ Pa, PsatB=10⁵ Pa; Pbubble=xA PA*+(1−xA) PB*; yA=xAPA*/Pbubble. Pdew=1/[yA/PA*+(1−yA)/PB*]. α=PA*/PB*. An x–y curve with constant α is a surrogate for a distillation exercise.
method: Evaluate bubble and dew branches at same fixed T. Lock the opposite composition. Analytic inverse ratio gives matched tie-line endpoints. Phase amount requires overall composition.
limits: Ideal liquid and vapour, nonreacting, synthetic Psat at fixed T; no numerical T–x–y curve from a single pair of constants. Next model γi(T,x) and licensed vapour-pressure fits with documented intervals.

relation: y*=αx/[1+(α−1)x]; xeq(y)=y/[α−(α−1)y]. Rectifying y=Rx/(R+1)+xD/(R+1); saturated-liquid q-line x=zF. Stripping line through (zF,yrect(zF)) and (xB,xB). Start (xD,xD), go horizontally to equilibrium then vertically to active line using x≥zF as rectifying. Stop after horizontal step reaches x≤xB.
method: Compute slope=(xD−yeq(zF))/(xD−zF), Rmin=slope/(1−slope); numeric .8 at defaults. Proceed only R>Rmin or an identified nonpinching boundary. Stage count includes last integer contact.
limits: Binary constant α, constant molar overflow, saturated liquid feed, total condenser, equilibrium stages. Require xB<zF<xD; Rmin from rectifying line through pinch (zF,y*(zF)) and (xD,xD) where physically admissible; block pinch or decreasing-step failure. Cap 500 stages and distinguish numerical cap from infeasibility.

relation: t=μRm V/(AΔp)+μαc V²/(2A²Δp); c is dry cake mass per filtrate volume. Write t=bv+av², v=V/A; stable v=2t/[b+√(b²+4at)], b=μRm/Δp, a=μαc/(2Δp). Areq=Vtarget/v. Instantaneous flux=Δp/[μ(Rm+αcv)].
method: Use stable positive quadratic inverse including a=0. At t=0 return zero volume and finite initial flux, t/V undefined. Round commercial areas upward only after solving continuous minimum.
limits: Constant pressure, Newtonian filtrate, incompressible homogeneous cake, constant retention; neglect startup hold-up and wash time. For compressible cake model α(Δp) with multiple-pressure data; invalid for cross-flow/TFF.

relation: Synthetic plant τdy/dt=−y+Kpu+d. Each sample e=r−y; D=−Kc Td (y−yprev)/Ts filtered with β=Tf/(Tf+Ts), Df=βDfprev+(1−β)D; uraw=Kc e+I+Df; u=clip(uraw,0,1). I_next=I+Ts[Kc e/Ti+(u−uraw)/Tt] when back-calculation enabled. Plant exact ZOH update y_next=Kpu+d+(y−Kpu−d)exp(−Ts/τ). τ=10 s, Kp=1, Tf=.5 s, Tt=2 s, Ts=.1 s. Normalised variables.
method: Apply sample order as specified; emit commanded/applied output at k and next PV at k+1; never retroactively recompute a recorded sample. Back-calculation correction is disabled only in the comparison preset.
limits: Linear first-order plant without transport delay; controller is positional with derivative on measurement. Fixed sample cadence independent of render. Define P/PI/PID presets by enabling terms; P only forces I=0. No hardware route.

relation: dy/dt=−λy, y(0)=1, exact exp(−λt); z=−λΔt; amplification Euler 1+z, backward Euler 1/(1−z), RK4 1+z+z²/2+z³/6+z⁴/24. Apply recurrence; shorten last step precisely to final T. Error against analytic value at same T.
method: Use exact analytic factors for this test equation; expose general RK stages in Explore. For convergence compare dt,dt/2,dt/4 and p=log₂(Eh/Eh/2), skip zero/roundoff. Bound work and terminate if values overflow.
limits: Smooth scalar linear IVP, fixed-step examples; Euler absolute stability requires 0<λΔt<2 for decay; 1<λΔt<2 gives alternating sign. Implicit stability does not guarantee accuracy.

relation: Teaching line y=a+bx+ε; use QR least squares on [1,x]. s²=SSE/(n−2); leverage h*=1/n+(x*−x̄)²/Sxx; 95% mean CI: ŷ±t(.975,n−2)s√h*; prediction interval uses √(1+h*). Extension quadratic fit via QR on centred/scaled x and independent hold-out residuals.
method: Centre/scale x and solve by QR. Use inverse Student-t with n−2 df or a vetted table in supported n range. Restore seed, generator version, train/test IDs and coefficients for repeatable runs.
limits: OLS assumes full-rank design, independent mean-zero homoscedastic errors; t-based intervals additionally assume normal errors. Range cannot establish correct functional form. Singular fits return reason. Imported data need units, origin and split metadata.

relation: Q=πD²v/4; gD=πDv/2, gv=πD²/4; u²Q=gD²uD²+gv²uv²+2r gD gv uD uv. First-order standard uncertainty. Compare Monte Carlo draws for D,v with specified joint normal model; label sampled central 95% coverage interval distinctly.
method: Use direct correlated draws D=D₀+uD z₁ and v=v₀+uv[r z₁+√(1−r²)z₂]; default 10000 seeded draws in worker. Screen normal tail probabilities P(D≤0) or P(v<0)>10⁻⁶ as product default; report draw count and model choice.
limits: Linearisation local to nominal point; joint-normal choice is a scenario assumption. If appreciable probability of D≤0 or v<0, disable normal MC or ask for a supported positive distribution; do not silently truncate. At |r|=1 handle singular covariance directly.

relation: y/y₀=(x/x₀)^n, exp(kx), or ln(x/x₀); x₀=y₀=1 and k=1 in scaled variables.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Fit a measured curve, inspect residuals outside training. Select log x only when all x>0.
limits: Log arguments must be dimensionless and positive. Straightness on transformed axes alone cannot identify a mechanism.

relation: f(x)=x²−s; bisect sign-changing brackets and compare Newton x←x−f/(2x).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Compare bisection ≤ceil(log₂(width/tol)) steps with safeguarded Newton. A multidimensional solve needs a Jacobian.
limits: An even-multiplicity root need not change sign; derivative zero invalidates Newton update. No real solution for s<0.

relation: For F,D,U,ρ,μ build column exponents in M,L,T; nullspace gives Π₁=F/(ρU²D²), Π₂=ρUD/μ. Rank three gives two independent groups.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use rational Gaussian elimination on dimension vectors; verify MLT products cancel; add gravity as independent variable to recover Froude scaling.
limits: Requires a physically complete variable set; equal Re alone cannot ensure equal Froude or surface-tension effects.

relation: For −kT″=qv, T(0)=T(L)=300, solve tridiagonal central differences; exact T=300+qv x(L−x)/(2k); k=1, L=1.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Tridiagonal O(N) solve. Use separate manufactured sinusoid, then variable k harmonic face coefficients and grid refinement.
limits: Constant source produces exact quadratic nodal values; use nonpolynomial manufactured solution for observed second-order convergence.

relation: Steady two-stream mix xout=(F₁x₁+F₂x₂)/(F₁+F₂); xB=1−xA. Batch addition uses masses instead of mass rates.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Add density for volumetric mixing and enthalpy for thermal coupling. Compare a weighed dilution with independent composition calibration.
limits: Fractions on matching basis, no reaction. Outlet composition undefined at zero total flow.

relation: Fresh A and inert I enter a first-order pass with fixed conversion X. Remove all product, return fraction 1−p of unreacted A and I. Aloop=FA/[1−(1−p)(1−X)]; Iloop=FI/p. Bypass alternative treats fraction b of fresh feed as untouched, Xoverall=(1−b)X at no recycle.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Extension solves simultaneous linear species balances for arbitrary split matrix; compare rank and measured purge composition.
limits: Steady finite solution requires a sink per fed component; restrict modes to depicted flowsheet.

relation: Parallel A→B and A→C, 1:1 stoichiometry; outlet A=FA0−ξB−ξC, yield on feed=ξB/FA0, selectivity=ξB/ξC.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. For an arbitrary reaction network construct stoichiometric matrix, check elemental conservation and feasible extents.
limits: FA0=1 mol/s; extents sum ≤feed. If ξC=0 distinguish unlimited selectivity from 0/0. Equal stoichiometric molar masses in teaching isomers.

relation: At fixed illustrative boiling point Tb=373 K, q=mcp(Tb−Ti)+mλf during boiling. For continuous flow replace mass by ṁ and energy by power. cp=4000 J/(kg K), λ=2e6 J/kg, Ti=293 K.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Replace constant cp with ∫cp dT, use documented saturation data and heat leak; inspect enthalpy balance.
limits: Pure synthetic material; adiabatic, constant pressure; stop at fully vaporised unless vapour cp provided.

relation: Ideal P=RT/v; van der Waals P=RT/(v−b)−a/v², Z=Pv/(RT). In reduced variables Pr=8Tr/(3vr−1)−3/vr², Z=(3/8)Pr vr/Tr.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Numerical comparison uses van der Waals Pr=8Tr/(3Vr−1)−3/Vr². Set Tr=1 for default, probe Vr>1/3; solve stable phase via equal area or fugacity.
limits: v>b; positive compressibility requires ∂P/∂v<0. Subcritical loops require phase equilibrium construction; cubic roots alone cannot select a physical phase.

relation: Ideal reversible polytrope PVⁿ=const, work by gas W=(P₂V₂−P₁V₁)/(1−n), n=1 gives P₁V₁ln(V₂/V₁). Irreversible step against constant external pressure uses W=Pext(V₂−V₁) and specified bath.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Ideal isothermal bath work comparison uses Pext=P₂, T=300 K and bath entropy −Q/T. For adiabats use γ=1.4 gas with cp,cv.
limits: Ideal gas, reversible adiabatic only if n=γ and Q=0; compare irreversible isothermal endpoints using bath entropy. P₁V₁=1000 J.

relation: Two-reservoir refrigerator: QH=QL+W, COP=QL/W, Sgen=QH/TH−QL/TL, reversible COP=TL/(TH−TL). Vapour-compression extension uses four state enthalpies with h₄=h₃ and COP=(h₁−h₄)/(h₂−h₁).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Add refrigerant state-property library and compressor efficiency; compare enthalpy balance against pressure and temperature measurements.
limits: Fixed QL=1000 W; reject negative Sgen beyond tolerance. A Carnot bound is not an equipment rating.

relation: Ideal gas A⇌B, initially A only, K=aB/aA=ξ/(1−ξ); ξ=K/(1+K). van ’t Hoff ln(K₂/K₁)=−ΔH/R(1/T₂−1/T₁).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. For multiple reactions solve Gibbs minimisation with nonnegative species and element constraints. Validate against mixture data.
limits: Ideal 1:1 reaction at fixed T, consistent standard states; no pressure shift for Δν=0. Thermodynamic extent alone says nothing about time.

relation: Illustrative symmetric Margules lnγ₁=A x₂², lnγ₂=A x₁². At fixed T, bubble P=ΣxᵢγᵢPᵢ*; yᵢ=xᵢγᵢPᵢ*/P. For ideal constant Ki ideal flash solve Σzᵢ(Kᵢ−1)/[1+β(Kᵢ−1)]=0 on [0,1].
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Check sign at both flash bracket endpoints before bisection. Phase-split systems need stability testing and fitted binary parameters.
limits: Use illustrative Psat pair from S22; flash preset K₁=2,K₂=.5. Composition-dependent Ki require simultaneous equilibrium and balances; no reuse of constant-K solver unmodified.

relation: Q=Cd A₂√[2Δp/(ρ(1−β⁴))], β=D₂/D₁. Distinguish tap differential from permanent head loss.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use discharge calibration against independent reference; incorporate expansion factor for gas in separate module.
limits: Teaching Cd only; actual meter standards specify taps, straight runs, beta and Re; gas expansion excluded. D₁=.05 m, ρ=1000 kg/m³.

relation: Power law τ=K sign(γ̇)∣γ̇∣ⁿ, ηapp=K∣γ̇∣ⁿ⁻¹. K has units Pa·sⁿ, changes meaning with n.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Fit K,n on measured shear range; introduce yield stress with Herschel–Bulkley and plateau with Carreau separately.
limits: K numerical value fixed to 1 in SI for each synthetic family; no low-shear plateau for n<1. Yield stress requires other law.

relation: Static circular capillary h=2σcosθ/(ρgr); p jump from curvature. Wide bath, atmospheric interface, ρ=1000 kg/m³, g=9.80665.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Full Young–Laplace boundary-value solve uses meniscus curvature and contact hysteresis.
limits: Equilibrium, small tube relative to capillary length, unknown wettability supplies unknown applicability. Near tube scale meniscus/weight corrections matter.

relation: Two parallel branches h=KᵢQᵢ² share head, Q₁+Q₂=Qtot. Identical pump curves combine Hseries(Q)=2Hp(Q), Hparallel(Q)=Hp(Q/2). Intersect with Hz+bQ².
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Take K₁=10⁶ s²/m⁵; use S09 teaching pump and system defaults for pump mode. General graphs solve node balances and loop energy residuals.
limits: Positive forward monotone curves only. Prevent parallel pump reverse flow guesses; unequal pumps require independent operating branches/check valves.

relation: For an open supply NPSHa=(ps_abs−pv)/(ρg)+zs−zp−hf,s; margin=NPSHa−NPSHr(Q).
method: Evaluate the material or energy balance in section C, branch on the feasibility conditions in I. Use the surface pressure, vapour pressure, suction loss and level controls as supplied quantities. Without a defined vendor NPSHr curve and service criterion, margin stays unknown.
limits: Use ρ=1000; NPSHr without defined vendor criterion and service margin is unknown. Report available head only; do not certify cavitation absence.

relation: Teaching hydraulic conductance G=Q/√Δp; inherent equal percentage G=Gmax R^(x−1). Installed Δptot=Δpv+bQ², so Q=√[Δptot/(1/G²+b)].
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Vendor liquid sizing checks choking, pressure recovery and cavitation per service and standard. Direct Δp tap data can calibrate installed curve.
limits: Synthetic Gmax=.0001 m³/(s√Pa), Δptot=10000 Pa. x=0 is minimum controllable point, not leak-tight closure. Rated Kv/Cv require unit conversion and vendor rules.

relation: Isentropic ideal-gas nozzle: p*/p₀=(2/(γ+1))^(γ/(γ−1)); ṁ/A=p₀√[2γ/(RT₀(γ−1))(r^(2/γ)−r^((γ+1)/γ))], r=max(pb/p₀,p*/p₀).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Add a real-gas property model and discharge coefficient once geometry is specified. Total pressure and temperature are reservoir conditions.
limits: Converging ideal nozzle, γ=1.4,R=287 J/(kg K),T₀=300 K,p₀=100 kPa absolute. No downstream shock prediction.

relation: For a rigid isolated sphere vt=(ρp−ρ)gd²/(18μ); Rep=ρvtd/μ; settling chamber cut size from H/vt=residence time.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Iterative drag balance for finite Re uses a documented Cd(Rep) and shape data; validate with a size distribution and density uncertainty.
limits: ρp=2500,ρ=1000 kg/m³, μ=.001 Pa·s; use Stokes only for Rep≤.1 as conservative product guard. Non-Stokes drag, hindered settling and size distributions need separate evidence.

relation: Ergun Δp/L=150μ(1−ε)²U/(ε³dp²)+1.75ρ(1−ε)U²/(ε³dp); onset balance Δp/L≈(ρs−ρ)(1−ε)g using bed voidage at onset.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Solve positive onset quadratic, feed geometry and independently measured voidage. Fluidised branch requires expansion and drag data.
limits: Uniform rigid spheres, fixed bed, no cohesive forces/wall effects. ρ=1000, ρs=2500 kg/m³, μ=.001. Expansion requires voidage/drag closure.

relation: Sphere R=(1/ri−1/ro)/(4πk); fin with insulated tip η=tanh(mL)/(mL), m²=hP/(kAc). Composite parallel k=φk₁+(1−φ)k₂; series k=1/(φ/k₁+(1−φ)/k₂).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Replace insulated fin tip with convective BC; temperature-dependent k or network discretisation for heterogeneous layers.
limits: ro>ri,k=1 W/(m K); spherical symmetry; fin constant section/h/k; ideal laminate bounds, no contact resistance.

relation: Surface to large isothermal surroundings q″=εσ(Ts⁴−Tsur⁴)+h(Ts−Ta); σ=5.670374419e−8. h is supplied, not predicted. Extension natural convection Ra=gβΔTL³/(να).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Add view factors/radiosity or an applicable natural convection law, with orientation and film properties. Ra remains unknown without inputs.
limits: Uniform diffuse grey surface, view factor one, Ta=Tsur=300 K. h geometry dependent; natural convection correlation needs orientation and boundary data.

relation: Saturated pure fluid utility ṁ=Q̇/hfg; for an isothermal condensing side Q̇=Ccold(Tsat−Tin)[1−exp(−UA/Ccold)].
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Replace isothermal utility with desuperheat/condense/subcool segments at documented pressure; include boiling-side regimes from approved data.
limits: Tsat=373 K,Tin=293 K,hfg=2e6 J/kg; negligible pressure loss, dry saturation. Boiling regimes and critical heat flux cannot be inferred from duty alone.

relation: J=kL(Ci−Cb). In common concentration units with equilibrium Cg,i=mCl,i, 1/Kg=1/kg+m/kl. Sh=kLchar/D, Sc=ν/D. Integrate flux across finite film for linear profile.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Choose gas bulk=2 and liquid bulk=.25 mol/m³ for default J=Kg(2−m×.25). Solve interface concentrations from same flux; extend to nonlinear equilibrium iteratively.
limits: Consistent concentration bases, linear equilibrium, dilute transfer, no reaction or Stefan flow. Heat/mass analogy needs matching BC and regimes.

relation: Humidity ratio W=.622 pv/(P−pv), pv=RH psat. Constant-rate solid drying t=Ms(X₀−Xc)/(ANc); falling-rate linear law N=Nc(X−Xe)/(Xc−Xe), integrate for time.
method: Evaluate the material or energy balance in section C, branch on the feasibility conditions in I. Apply the fixed psychrometric and drying properties in section I. Integrate constant and falling-rate segments separately and join at Xc; use measured equilibrium moisture and drying data to replace the teaching law.
limits: P=100000 Pa, psat=3000 Pa at illustrative fixed T; Ms=A=1 SI, Nc=.001 kg/(m² s), X₀=.5,Xc=.2,Xe=.02. Do not equate humidity ratio to RH.

relation: Batch A→B→C, dA/dt=−k₁A, dB/dt=k₁A−k₂B, C=A₀−A−B. For k₁=k₂=k, B=A₀kt exp(−kt).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. General consecutive reactions integrate by RK4 or adaptive solver, verify equal-rate analytic limit and compare independently measured species.
limits: Irreversible isothermal homogeneous reactions, A₀=1 mol/m³. Changing order changes units of k. Cumulative intermediate peaks before final conversion.

relation: N equal CSTRs in series: E(t)=(N/τ)^N t^(N−1)exp(−Nt/τ)/(N−1)!; mean τ, variance τ²/N. Measured E=C/∫Cdt after baseline subtraction for constant flow pulse.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use log-gamma or bounded factorial for tanks in series; integrate measured traces by trapezoids, compare recovered tracer mass against dose.
limits: Mass recovery and finite sampling window matter; RTD alone rarely identifies a unique topology. An input pulse of finite duration requires convolution.

relation: Dimensionless material and energy balances dc/ds=1−c−Da exp(θ)c, dθ/ds=−θ+B Da exp(θ)c−H(θ−θc). Local exponential sensitivity is an illustrative approximation. Find steady branches by continuation, test Jacobian eigenvalues.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Bracket reduced 1D residual via c=1/(1+Da exp θ); additionally search tangencies by derivative turning points. Numerical trajectories require bounded stiff integration.
limits: Synthetic dimensionless local teaching model, θc=0, c(0)=1, θ(0)=0. Large θ invalidates local law; bounded domain and stop on solver failure.

relation: First-order isothermal sphere φ=R√(k/De), η=(3/φ²)(φ cothφ−1). Near zero use η≈1−φ²/15. Internal concentration profile C/Cs=sinh(φr/R)/[(r/R)sinhφ].
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Check small and large φ limits; external film or nonisothermal catalyst needs an additional boundary balance.
limits: Uniform effective diffusion, no external film, no thermal gradients; intrinsic k independent of pellet size. Use analytic centre limit.

relation: Dilute constant-flow absorber Z=HTU·NTU, HTU=Gm/(Kya) using consistent molar-flux and mole-fraction driving-force basis; NTU=∫dy/(y−y*). A=V̇g/us; D=√(4A/π).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Solve nonzero equilibrium by quadrature and detect pinch; supplier capacity and measured mass-transfer coefficients needed for real packing.
limits: Dilute strong-solvent limit y*=0 in starter, HTU=1 m, gas flow=1 m³/s; flooding, wetting, distribution and pressure drop require packing-specific vendor data.

relation: One ideal dilute stage solute fraction remaining f=L/(L+KS); N equal fresh-solvent crosscurrent stages leave [L/(L+KS/N)]^N.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Add cross-solubility and ternary tie lines or countercurrent stage balances; new data determine phase split.
limits: Carrier mass flow L=1 kg/s; immiscible carriers, dilute solute, each stage reaches equilibrium. Emulsification and mutual solubility require ternary data.

relation: Langmuir q=qmax bC/(1+bC). Ideal sharp-front service time t=M[q(Cin)−q(0)]/(Q Cin) neglecting fluid inventory. A finite front requires dispersion, bed voidage and transfer kinetics.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. A later advection–dispersion and kinetic adsorption model needs isotherm, bed density, flow and column data. Fit equilibrium and validate breakthrough separately.
limits: qmax=1 mol/kg, Q=.001 m³/s; equilibrium capacity gives an ideal limit, cannot predict measured breakthrough shape.

relation: J=(TMP−Δπ)/[μ(Rm+Rf)], TMP=(pfeed+pret)/2−pperm; A=Qp/J. For complete rejection film limit Jlim=k ln(Cg/Cb) is a separate constraint with a different mechanism.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Treat averaged TMP as a reduction of axial pressure data; add axial crossflow, retentate concentration and resistance evolution with new measurements.
limits: μ=.001, Rm=1e12 m⁻¹, Δπ=0 for starter water; constant resistance only. No assumption of a fouling trajectory or limiting flux without concentration data.

relation: Feed F, nonvolatile solute fraction xf. Evaporate E of pure solvent, then ideal crystals P satisfy Fxf=P+(F−E−P)xs at specified saturation. Q̇ideal=Eλ for saturated inlet.
method: Evaluate the material or energy balance in section C, branch on the feasibility conditions in I. Use the design basis in D and I; E must be less than feed mass and cannot exceed available solvent. Compare zero crystals when undersaturated and the stated positive result after concentrating. Add a population balance only with kinetic data.
limits: λ=2e6 J/kg, no entrainment, pure dry crystals, saturated feed temperature, solubility supplied. For unsaturated concentrate return zero crystals and actual mother liquor fraction; no negative mass.

relation: Ideal Σ model Qcap=vgΣ; vg from Stokes S49; optional radial drift dr/dt=Δρd²ω²r/(18μ), travel time ∝ln(ro/ri).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Capture curve needs feed PSD, bowl geometry and validated equivalent area. Verify gravity model independently before substituting centrifugal acceleration.
limits: Ideal dilute classification; Σ convention depends on machine and efficiency. Compressible biological solids and depth filters require measured capacity curves.

relation: First-order G=K exp(−θs)/(1+τs); step after delay K[1−exp(−(t−θ)/τ)], impulse K exp(−(t−θ)/τ)/τ. Second-order G=Kωn²/(s²+2ζωns+ωn²); integrating G=K/s. Bode magnitude 20log10∣G(jω)∣, phase unwrap separately.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use exact transfer functions and compare a time-integrated sinusoid after transients. Complex poles require second-order solver or analytic branches by damping.
limits: K=1 in normalised variables, ωn=1 rad/s; ideal LTI models, fixed operating point. Integrator has no finite step steady state.

relation: Two-stream blend y=(F₁c₁+F₂c₂)/(F₁+F₂); ratio station F₂,sp=rF₁; installed cascade inner flow τi Ḟ₂=u−F₂, outer blend τo ẏ=yblend−y. Feedforward ideal F₂=F₁(c₁−ysp)/(ysp−c₂). Split-range maps one signed demand to heating or cooling with deadband.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use separate state for inner tracking and outer inventory; S25 controller kernel for outer feedback. Saturation active in all topologies.
limits: c₁=1,c₂=0, τi=1 s, τo=10 s; secondary loop must be faster and measurable. Split-range is a separate signed utility scenario.

relation: Discrete normalised plant yₖ₊₁=a yₖ+(1−a)uₖ. Receding horizon minimise Σ[(y−r)²+λΔu²] with 0≤u≤1, ∣Δu∣≤.2. For starter enumerate move sequences on {.0,.2,…,1.0}, apply first move, repeat.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Enumerate only rate-feasible moves and use lexicographic smallest first move on ties. Later use a bounded quadratic programme, tracking data and model mismatch evidence.
limits: Known linear plant, sample 1 s, y₀=u₋₁=0, r=1. Complexity ≤6ᴺ, cap horizon; real-time Master use requires separate engineering review.

relation: τs ẏm=y+b−ym; τa u̇a=uc−ua; additive seeded sensor noise; stuck sensor freezes observation only. Independent ideal plant first-order state retained.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Piecewise exact ZOH or RK4 with event boundaries, seed noise as in standard. Validate isolated sensor and drive responses before fault inference.
limits: Normalised teaching plant, initial zero. Identical observation traces can have multiple causes; assess ability to propose a discriminating test.

relation: Generic nonpathogenic teaching biomass: μ=μmax S/(Ks+S); batch dX/dt=μX, dS/dt=−μX/Y; optional product dP/dt=αμX with synthetic yield. For fed-batch use inventories VX,VS and dV/dt=F; continuous mode includes outlet inventories.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use an adaptive integrator with substrate depletion event; extension add volume balance or measured product stoichiometry. Compare fit on separate teaching runs.
limits: Uniform synthetic food-yeast analogy, no strain-specific cultivation parameters. First design exercise uses closed balance; kinetics and yields would need independent measurement.

relation: Scaled nonwashout S*=D Ks/(μmax−D), X*=Y(Sin−S*); washout X=0, S=Sin. Critical D=μ(Sin) under stated no-decay model.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Check physical feasibility before selecting steady branch. Later integrate start-up from finite biomass and include independently measured decay.
limits: Ideal nonpathogenic teaching balance, sterile feed, no retention/decay, no organism-specific operating prescription. At D=0 the steady-state branch is degenerate; show batch mode.

relation: dC/dt=kLa(C*−C)−OUR; constant demand gives Css=C*−OUR/kLa; if C reaches zero stop demand-only branch and flag missing oxygen-limited kinetics.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Exact first-order propagation between changes. Fit kLa and probe lag with separately characterised sensor; demand may depend on oxygen concentration.
limits: C*=.25 mol/m³, C₀=.25; constant supply/demand teaching model. Volumetric coefficient lumped; aeration/agitation alone do not establish it. Heat generation requires measured heat per substrate.

relation: v=Vmax S/(Km+S), v/Vmax=s/(1+s), s=S/Km; apply initial-rate assumption and fit untransformed residuals for extended investigation.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Add inhibition or progress-curve fitting only with evidence; use nonlinear regression on measured rates rather than reciprocal-error distortion.
limits: Single-substrate initial-rate model without inhibition or transport limitation. At all S≪Km only Vmax/Km identifiable.

relation: Two Gaussian peaks with baseline widths wi=4σi; Rs=2(tR2−tR1)/(w1+w2), area-normalised Gaussian concentration signal. N=(tR/σ)² for ideal plate model.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Gaussian full-domain reference; compare tailing residuals before choosing exponentially modified Gaussian or transport model.
limits: Symmetric ideal analytical peaks; retention times exceed widths to avoid significant negative-time tails. Overloading and asymmetric tails require a transport model.

relation: Reimp=ρND²/μ, P=NpρN³D⁵, tip speed πND, V=πT²H/4. Compare scale rules constant P/V, tip speed or Re for geometrically similar tanks.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Add Np(Re) for each impeller, baffling and clearance; require mixing-time tracer and power measurements on a held-out geometry.
limits: Teaching Np=5 constant only where supported by a geometry-specific turbulent plateau; ρ=1000, μ=.001, T=3D,H=T. No predicted mixing time, oxygen transfer or heat removal from Np alone; add tracer t95 and measured kLa independently.

relation: Cooling water ṁ=Q̇/(cpΔT); ideal pump energy E=Pshaft t; purchased energy=E/ηmotor; annual illustrative cost=unit tariff×kWh. Vessel working volume V=Qτ, total=V/fill.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use independent design basis for residence vessel; assumed fill=.8, Q=.001 m³/s, τ=100 s. Costing optional when dated tariff supplied.
limits: cp=4000 J/(kg K), ηmotor=.8, Pshaft=800 W for separate starter; posted sliders in hours converted to seconds internally. Installed cost only with dated local pricing, capacity and scope.

relation: For uₜ+a uₓ=0 with periodic BC, upwind Uⱼⁿ⁺¹=Uⱼⁿ−C(Uⱼⁿ−Uⱼ₋₁ⁿ), C=aΔt/Δx for a>0. Exact translation of a smooth periodic pulse. Separately compare linear finite elements for steady 1D diffusion using local k/ℓ [[1,−1],[−1,1]].
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Default periodic field 1+.5sin(2πx/L). For FE compare assembled 1D steady source with S32. F5 requires validated specialist solver and mesh evidence.
limits: L=1 m,a=1 m/s; conservative periodic stencil. Teaching window for stability 0≤C≤1; above it mark divergent numerical experiment. F5 is comparison target only.

relation: Empirical constant-pressure capacity model t/V=1/Q₀+t/Vmax for cumulative filtrate V. V=t/(1/Q₀+t/Vmax); normalise Q₀ and Vmax by area for scale transfer.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Differentiate to get J=J₀/(1+J₀t/vmax)². Fit several pilot curves and compare independent lot throughput; evaluate breakthrough separately.
limits: Synthetic fouling law only; no universal filtration claim. Clarification quality, feed variability and independently measured endpoints are additional constraints.

relation: One shell pass, even tube passes: ε=2/[1+Cr+S coth(NTU S/2)], S=√(1+Cr²); Q̇=ε Cmin ΔTin. At NTU=0 use ε=0. Rf″ on a common area changes Udirty.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Cmin=1000 W/K, ΔTin=50 K for watts. Compare with independent LMTD correction-factor source for same configuration.
limits: Constant properties, ideal shell-side mixing assumptions. Leakage, bypass, vibration and actual geometry require vendor rating. Dirty NTU=N/(1+β).

relation: Local Clausius–Clapeyron approximation ln(P₂/P₁)=−ΔHvap/R(1/T₂−1/T₁). General dP/dT=ΔH/(TΔv). Preset ΔHvap=40000 J/mol, T₁=350 K, P₁=100000 Pa.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use measured ΔH(T), actual phase volumes or named property package for broader T; check derivative and critical region separately.
limits: Ideal vapour, negligible liquid molar volume, constant latent heat; local approximation only. Critical and triple points require actual property data.

relation: Compare normalised illustrative power profile u/Umax=(1−r/R)^(1/n) with laminar profile. Area mean/Umax=2n²/[(n+1)(2n+1)]. Exact developed-pipe wall stress magnitude τw=DΔp/(4L).
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Integrate 2r-weighted profile numerically; for real wall stress use pressure taps or wall model with viscous sublayer.
limits: Empirical outer-shape approximation cannot provide finite wall gradient; centreline slope also imperfect. D=.05 m,L=10 m. For viscous sublayer need wall units and independent friction velocity.

relation: At imposed Q, Δp=μ(Q/A)[Rm+αc Qt/A]; tstop=(Δplimit−μJRm)/(μαcJ²) for J=Q/A. Stop immediately if initial pressure already exceeds limit.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Analytic pressure growth; when pressure ceiling below initial requirement mark infeasible. Compare pressure-ramp measurements independent of fit.
limits: μ=.001, Rm=1e10 m⁻¹, α=1e10 m/kg, c=10 kg/m³. Constant cake resistance and no compression or pump slip.

relation: For an isolated spherical drop teaching form Sh=2+.6 Re^½ Sc^⅓, k=Sh Dm/d; analogous heat transfer Nu=2+.6 Re^½ Pr^⅓. Distinguish the diffusion-only intercept from forced convection.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Set Pr=Sc in the explicitly analogous scenario, compare separate coefficients and units. Resolve original fit envelope before any numeric design use.
limits: Single sphere, small transfer rate, constant external conditions, negligible deformation/interactions. Release range restricted to original checked data; supplied interface domain is an exploration box only.

relation: Fit a first-order tracer envelope e(t)=∣C−C∞∣/∣C₀−C∞∣=exp(−t/τm); t95=τm ln20. Separate energy balance ρcp V dT/dt=Qgen−UA(T−Tc); Qgen specified, not inferred from agitation.
method: Evaluate the governing relationship in section C using the selected mode. Use measured probe locations and sustained tolerance criterion; require ρcpV before transient thermal calculation. Additional scale data can justify multi-zone model.
limits: Teaching exponential assumes monotone well-mixed response; local recirculation may cross tolerance repeatedly. Use sustained entry for noisy data. Heat response uses uniform bulk and steady coolant.
